what_its_for: Fosinopril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure. It belongs to a group of medicines called ACE inhibitors. It works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood.
how_to_take: Take fosinopril by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 10 mg once a day. For heart failure, the usual starting dose is 10 mg once a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time up to 40 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose without talking to them first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fosinopril at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as fosinopril can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid anti-inflammatory pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) without asking your doctor first, as they may make fosinopril less effective and harm your kidneys. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of the following: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this can be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); trouble breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice your blood pressure improving within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. For heart failure, it may take several weeks to feel the full effects. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking fosinopril without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take fosinopril if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as it is not known if fosinopril passes into breast milk. Older adults: If you are 65 or older, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely, as you may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and at higher risk for dizziness and falls. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver problems. Children: The safety and effectiveness of fosinopril in children under 6 years old or children with kidney problems has not been established.
